findings.title: Leftover debug logging at Error level dumps every ID batch
findings.body: Every cleanup batch logs at Error level, both before and after the delete. Each entry includes the full `ids` slice, which can hold up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize entries (tens of thousands), plus the raw SQL condition. The `err` field is always nil at the point it is logged. The same happens at lines 537, 554, 557, 576 and 579. In production this floods logs with huge lines and raises false Error alerts on every run, even when nothing failed. These look like debugging leftovers and should be removed, or reduced to Debug level without the ID list.

findings.title: Cleanup interval silently changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: The ticker for the whole CleanUpService was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute. This change is unrelated to the deadlock fix and is not mentioned in the description. It makes every cleanup job run 10x more often across all instances: snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs and query history. That adds DB load and more chances for the very lock contention this PR tries to reduce. It also no longer matches the 9-minute per-run timeout, which was sized for a 10-minute interval. This looks like a debugging leftover and should be reverted.

findings.title: Quadratic string building for inlined SQLite ID list
findings.body: In the SQLite large-batch path, the IN list is built with `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` in a loop. This copies the whole growing string on every iteration, so cost is O(n^2) in the batch size. For the batch sizes this path targets (e.g. 32767 IDs), that means hundreds of MB of copying per batch. Use a strings.Builder or strconv.AppendInt into a byte slice instead, as is already done in getAccessControlFilter.

findings.title: Placeholder path can exceed MySQL/Postgres bind-parameter limits
findings.body: For non-SQLite databases, the delete always binds one placeholder per ID. Both MySQL and PostgreSQL cap prepared statements at 65535 parameters. With an AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize above that, every delete batch fails and cleanup never makes progress. The old single-statement subquery had no such limit. Either chunk the IDs, or use the inlined-integer approach for any batch above the dialect's limit.
